chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Multazam: 'For which thing is it adhered to, and which thing is mentioned therein?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By it is a river from the rivers of Paradise, in which are cast the deeds of the servants, every Thursday.'

key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَم: The section of the Kaaba's wall adhered to during supplication, located between the door and the Yemeni corner

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Al-Multazam and what happens there on Thursdays?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reveals the metaphysical reality of Al-Multazam as a conduit for divine mercy, where a river from Paradise receives the deeds of worshippers every Thursday. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Kaaba not merely as a geometric center but as a spiritual axis where earthly worship intersects with celestial recording, reinforcing the virtue of specific times and locations in enhancing one's spiritual state.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about Al-Multazam (the back part of the Kabah), ‘For which thing is it adhered to, and which thing is mentioned therein?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By it is a river from the rivers of the Paradise, in which are cast the deeds of the servants, every Thursday’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Multazam, for what reason it is held and what is said in it. He (the Imam) said, ‘Nearby there is a canal of the canals of paradise in which the deeds of the servants (of Allah) are thrown every Thursday.’”
